params.predicate: The excerpt identifies a concrete limitation of an existing approach and explains a causal reason or operating circumstance that produces it. Generic needs for better performance, a list of applications, or an unexplained statement that prior art is deficient are insufficient. Use only the supplied excerpt; missing or unstated evidence means False.

The excerpt specifies all three: an observed or predicted quantity; comparison with a reference, target, or loss objective; and adjustment of a physical control parameter or learned model parameter to reduce the discrepancy. Diagnosis, notification, display, or resource routing without a corrective parameter adjustment is insufficient. Use only the supplied excerpt; missing or unstated evidence means False.

params.instr: In 100-160 words identify the observable, comparator, adjusted parameter, and target of correction. Explain whether there is corrective actuation, diagnosis only, or no comparison; include supporting phrases. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.

params.predicate: An observed signal, extracted feature, measured quantity, or computed resource requirement is explicitly used to determine a diagnostic result, select processing, or change an operating action. Exclude fixed processing sequences without such a decision, permission/token checks, and selection based only on a user's command. Use only the supplied excerpt; missing or unstated evidence means False.

params.instr: Extract observable -> decision rule -> resulting action in 30-60 words. Explicitly distinguish automatic decisions from user commands and static arrangements. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.

State the object acted on and the intervention level (material, component, device, process, or system) in at most 20 words. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.
